answer.label: Not Kurt Vonnegut — actually comedian Emo Philips
answer.sourceLine: This is a stand-up one-liner, not a line from any Vonnegut book. Quote Investigator traces it to surreal comedian Emo Philips, whose act contained the joke by November 1985 ↗. The Vonnegut credit only surfaced in a 2007 newspaper obituary sidebar and “has no substantive support.”

source.heading: Where it really comes from
source.excerpt: How many people here tonight are telekinetic? Raise my hand.
trail: Quote Investigator ↗ dates the joke to a November 1985 profile of Emo Philips and calls him the leading candidate to have created it.
The same investigation records the drift of credit over time: to Steven Wright by 1998, then to Kurt Vonnegut only in a May 2007 newspaper sidebar published after Vonnegut’s death.
Sites such as Goodreads ↗ still file the paraphrase “Those who believe in telekinetics, raise my hand” under Vonnegut with no source.
source.excerptNote: The earliest documented wording, from Emo Philips’ act in 1985, ran “How many people here have telekinetic powers? … Raise my hand!” The joke circulates in many near-identical variants.

source.rightsNote: The line is a modern stand-up joke documented from November 1985, well after 1931, so it is treated as in-copyright to its author, Emo Philips. (The copyright status of spoken stand-up material is itself unsettled, but nothing here is public domain and it is certainly not Vonnegut’s.)

author.name: Emo Philips
author.heading: About Emo Philips
author.bio: Emo Philips (born Phil Soltanec, February 7, 1956) is an American comedian known for a surreal, childlike stage persona and paraprosdokian one-liners delivered in a wandering falsetto. A cult figure of the 1980s comedy scene, he is celebrated for jokes that swap a predictable punchline for a grim or absurd twist — exactly the shape of the telekinesis gag. His act was widely covered in the mid-1980s, including a 1985 profile that captured this very line.

misattribution.heading: How Vonnegut got the credit
misattribution.intro: This is a comedian’s one-liner that migrated onto a beloved author. Quote Investigator followed the paper trail and found the credit drifting across three famous names.

items.why: The Vonnegut credit surfaces only in a May 2007 sidebar in The Courier (Iowa) reviewing his life just after his death; per Quote Investigator ↗ it “has no substantive support” and appears in none of his books. The paraphrase “Those who believe in telekinetics, raise my hand” is now pinned to him on Goodreads ↗.

The joke was ascribed to deadpan comedian Steven Wright by 1998; it fits his style, but the 13-year gap after the 1985 Emo Philips citation makes it unlikely, and Wright is himself a known quotation magnet, per Quote Investigator ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: The leading candidate to have created the joke is comedian Emo Philips, whose act contained it by November 1985 ↗ — years before either famous author was ever credited.

context.heading: Why the joke sticks
lead: The gag is a paraprosdokian: “How many people here tonight are telekinetic?” sets up a show-of-hands, then “Raise my hand” yanks the logic sideways — if telekinesis were real, the audience could move the speaker’s hand. That compressed self-referential twist is the signature of Emo Philips’ writing.
It reads as “Vonnegut-ish” because Vonnegut prized dry, deflating one-liners — which is exactly why a stray obituary sidebar could glue a comedian’s bit to him and have it stick.
context.pull: If telekinesis were real, you’d raise his hand.
